PullRequest.Title: build: Update all Component Explorer packages
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

Update every Component Explorer dependency to the current `next` release, retaining the repository's existing prerelease channel and caret ranges:

| Package | Previous | Updated |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `@vscode/component-explorer` | `0.2.1-140` | `0.2.1-160` |
| `@vscode/component-explorer-cli` | `0.2.1-143` | `0.2.1-162` |
| `@vscode/component-explorer-webpack-plugin` | `0.3.1-132` | `0.3.1-152` |
| `@vscode/component-explorer-vite-plugin` | `0.2.1-140` | `0.2.1-160` |

Updates the root, Rspack, and Vite manifests and their lockfiles. No unrelated dependency or source changes.

## Validation

Revalidated after refreshing to the versions above:

- `npm run compile` passed.
- Rspack static Component Explorer build passed (`COMPONENT_EXPLORER_STATIC_BUILD=1`, `npm exec -- rspack build --config rspack.serve-out.config.mts` from `build/rspack`).
- Updated CLI rendered `platform/buttonBar/Buttons/Dark` and `platform/buttonBar/Buttons/Light`: both reported `hasError: false` and produced non-empty screenshots.
- `npm ls` confirmed all four package versions and consistent explorer peer resolution across all three manifests.
- `npm run precommit` completed successfully against the staged files; these JSON files are excluded from file-level hygiene checks.
- `git diff --check` passed.

**Existing validation limitation:** `npm run build` in `build/vite` still fails with 13 `builtin:vite-json` parsing errors. During initial validation, reproduced this failure with the original explorer and Vite plugin versions (`0.2.1-140`) as well. This unrelated Vite build issue is not changed here.

Scenarios.Scenario: Cold or cached dependency installation for the root, Rspack, and Vite workspaces
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each workspace's npm ci must resolve and extract its locked Component Explorer packages before build or test jobs can proceed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch locked npm tarballs on a cache miss.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to the changed package artifacts needed by each npm ci, with the shared explorer artifact reusable through npm's cache; no additional dependency node is added.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The prior versions required the same package identities and the same direct/transitive dependency graph, also fetched on cold-cache misses.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: A cold install waits for missing artifacts; a warm install does not perform these fetches.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Extract package files into each workspace's node_modules tree.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: The same package-node count as before across the three workspaces.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The previous exact versions were extracted into the same workspace locations; the supplied diff provides no package-size evidence of increased bytes or files.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Extraction is on the install critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Five changed package identities across three manifests; @vscode/component-explorer is repeated in all three installations but can reuse npm's shared download cache.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Concurrency and download scheduling remain owned by npm; the diff adds no loop, Promise fan-out, limiter, queue, or additional package node.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold npm cache may fetch the new tarballs; a warm cache reuses integrity-addressed artifacts. The lockfiles preserve the same package/dependency topology and only replace versions, URLs, and integrity hashes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that package count, dependency topology, and install boundary cardinality are unchanged; no confidence-supported evidence shows the replacement tarballs add meaningful installation cost.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The tarball contents and compressed/uncompressed sizes are not present in the supplied repository diff, so version-specific byte differences cannot be measured.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: changing exact package artifacts creates ordinary cache misses after an upgrade, but the diff does not increase package cardinality or establish increased bytes, CPU, I/O, or concurrency.

Scenarios.Scenario: Rspack Component Explorer development serve and static CI build
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Rspack loads ComponentExplorerPlugin, discovers src/**/*.fixture.ts, bundles the workbench and fixtures, and emits or serves the result before screenshot rendering can begin.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run the Rspack build or dev server process.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One static build per component-fixtures job or one long-lived dev server per CSS-order scan.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same commands and process cardinality used the previous explorer and webpack-plugin versions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The build/server must become ready before fixtures can be rendered.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Glob fixture sources, read the transitive module/CSS graph, and emit build assets.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One unchanged src/**/*.fixture.ts discovery scope followed by the existing module graph; static output is emitted once.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The previous plugin received the identical include pattern and build configuration; no changed package dependency or repository code proves additional scans or repeated work.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Discovery and bundling are on build startup and compilation's critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The repository's fixture-file set and transitive module graph; the include pattern remains one repository-wide fixture glob.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Rspack controls module-build concurrency. The static workflow invokes one build, while the CSS scan starts one long-lived dev server; the diff adds no parallel build or scan.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: A clean CI build has no prior output cache in this configuration; the CSS-order workflow keeps one running server and reuses it across render probes. The plugin configuration and reuse behavior are unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the repository call path, fixture cardinality, and unchanged boundary placement; insufficient evidence of any version-specific expensive mechanism.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The external package implementations for the old and new prereleases are not included, so internal algorithm changes cannot be compared from this diff.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the dependency version changes expose the same single plugin invocation and same fixture glob, without diff evidence of added scans, serialization, retention, or build fan-out.

Scenarios.Scenario: Vite Component Explorer development server and build
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Vite initializes the Component Explorer plugin, discovers ../../src/**/*.fixture.ts with build mode all, and bundles or serves the workbench.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Discover fixture files and read/transform their module graph.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One unchanged glob over ../../src/**/*.fixture.ts per configured Vite startup/build.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The old Vite plugin was invoked once with the same include and build=all options.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Plugin initialization and required transforms precede a usable build/server.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serve generated modules and assets over the local Vite HTTP server.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Requests are driven by the same browser/client module graph; the diff changes no route or request loop in repository code.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same local server path existed with the previous plugin version.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Local requests are on interactive development-page loading paths.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: All matching fixture files and their imported module graph; the include and build options are unchanged.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Vite/Rolldown owns transform concurrency; one configured plugin instance runs in one dev-server or build process.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Vite may reuse its normal transform cache during a warm dev session; the diff does not alter keys, invalidation, include patterns, or server lifetime.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that repository-level invocation count and scaling inputs are unchanged; no concrete regression mechanism is visible.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No old/new plugin source or benchmark is supplied, so transform-time differences inside the external package are unknown.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: only the package versions change, while plugin cardinality, configuration, cache ownership, and repository boundaries remain the same.

Scenarios.Scenario: Component fixture screenshot rendering, Playwright tests, and scheduled CSS-order scanning
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The CLI serve/render path starts or attaches to the Rspack server, drives browser rendering, writes screenshots/manifests, and returns results. The CSS scan performs two full-fixture renders and then sequential O(log stylesheet-count) probes for each order-dependent fixture.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Invoke the Component Explorer CLI render command and, for configured serve, npm run serve-out-rspack; the CLI drives a browser process.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Component fixture CI uses one render invocation for all fixtures. CSS scanning uses two all-fixture invocations plus sequential logarithmic probes per changed candidate; this is pre-existing script structure.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The previous CLI version was called from the same sites with identical arguments and multiplicity.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Each invocation and browser render must complete before its manifest can be consumed; CSS probes are deliberately sequential.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Use local HTTP between the CLI/browser and the Rspack Component Explorer server.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Requests scale with rendered fixtures and navigations under the existing CLI; the repository diff adds no request or per-fixture call site.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same local server URLs and render workflow existed before the version update.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Local page and asset loads are required for each render.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Write screenshots and manifest files, then read manifests and copy/report selected images.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Images scale with rendered fixtures; report copies scale with order-dependent candidates. Hash-path deduplication remains enabled for probe renders.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The prior CLI and unchanged scripts used the same targets, manifest reads, image deduplication option, and report-copy loop.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Manifest reads gate result processing; image/report writes are part of completing CI artifacts.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize render input JSON and parse manifest JSON.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One small input serialization and one manifest parse per Renderer.render invocation; all-fixture manifests scale with fixture count as before.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical repository code serialized inputs and parsed manifests for the old CLI.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Parsing follows each render before the scan can continue.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: All matching fixtures for CI screenshot capture and the CSS scan; for each detected candidate, probe count scales logarithmically with its stylesheet document count. Playwright test files are fully parallel under the existing runner setting.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The config retains worktree maxSlots=1; cssOrderScan awaits the two full renders and each candidate/probe sequentially. Playwright's existing fullyParallel setting is unchanged. The diff adds no aggregate concurrency or missing limiter.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The serve process is reused for CSS probes, while each Renderer.render intentionally spawns a fresh CLI render/navigation and uses hash paths to deduplicate identical images where requested. This lifecycle and reuse policy are unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the pre-existing process, local HTTP, filesystem, serialization, fixture cardinality, sequential scan behavior, and maxSlots limit; there is no changed-line evidence that these costs increased.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The new CLI/runtime package internals are external to the supplied diff, so any implementation-level browser, IPC, network, or serialization changes cannot be established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: all observable boundary placement and multiplicity come from unchanged scripts/configuration. A version bump alone cannot prove added per-fixture work, concurrency, retention, or latency.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all six changed manifests/lockfiles and traced install, Rspack, Vite, CLI render, Playwright, and CSS-scan paths. The PR replaces external prerelease artifacts while preserving package count, dependency topology, plugin configuration, fixture cardinality, cache ownership, process count, and repository-level boundary scheduling. With no old/new package implementation or measured mechanism in the supplied diff, no actionable diff-caused performance regression is provable, and no regression-fix signal is established.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
